chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam said, 'I heard Safwan ibn Yahya saying,'

I said to al-Rida (peace be upon him), 'A man from your followers commanded me to ask you about a matter; he feared you and felt shy to ask you himself.' He (the Imam) said, 'What is it?' I said, 'A man comes to his wife in her anus.' He (the Imam) said, 'It is up to him.' I said to him, 'And do you do so?' He (the Imam) said, 'We do not do so.'

key_terms.الرِّضَا: Al-Rida (the eighth Imam, Ali ibn Musa)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on anal intercourse with one's wife in Shia Islam according to Imam al-Rida?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the distinction between legal permissibility (jawaz) and recommended practice (istihbab) in Shia jurisprudence, where Imam al-Rida (AS) confirms the act is valid but personally avoids it as a sign of modesty or preference. The chain of transmission through Safwan ibn Yahya, a prominent companion of the Imams, underscores the reliability of this ruling within the early scholarly tradition. It serves as a foundational text for understanding that while the act is not forbidden, the Imams often modeled restraint and elegance in marital relations.

en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from who has said, ‘I heard Safwan ibn Yahya who has said the following: “I once said to al-Rida’,

‘Alayhi al-Salam, that one of his followers has asked me to ask you a question in which he feels shy and intimidated. He (the Imam) asked, ‘What is the question?’ I asked, ‘Can a man come to his wife in her anus?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘It is up to him.’ I then asked, ‘Do you do so?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘No, we do not do so.’”
